Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Food glut: Annoh-Dompreh demands emergency government purchase of surplus produce Source : Myjoyonline.com 28 November 2026 9:45am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Minority Chief Whip Frank Annoh-Dompreh has called for emergency government intervention to buy surplus produce as farmers and market women struggle to find buyers nationwide.
The Nsawam-Adoagyiri MP warned that the growing food glut could undermine agricultural production, deepen rural poverty, and trigger a food shortage if the government does not act immediately.
Delivering a statement on the floor of Parliament today, Mr Annoh-Dompreh urged the government to deploy the National Food Buffer Stock Company (NAFCO) and other relevant institutions to absorb excess produce and protect farmers from mounting financial losses.
“Government, through NAFCO and other appropriate institutions, should purchase verified surplus commodities at transparent and economically sustainable prices, with clear regional targets and prompt payment to farmers.”
He said farmers who had invested borrowed funds and scarce resources in producing maize, rice, cassava, yam and soya beans were struggling to recover their investments.
Market women, he added, were equally distressed as consumers lacked the purchasing power to buy their produce.
“A farmer who cannot sell cannot repay loans, pay workers or finance the next planting season. A trader whose goods remain unsold loses working capital, while perishable produce deteriorates.
“If farmers respond by reducing production or abandoning agriculture, today’s glut could become tomorrow’s food shortage.”
Mr Annoh-Dompreh questioned the effectiveness of existing interventions, citing media reports that only about 40,000 to 44,000 metric tonnes of NAFCO’s 129,000 metric tonnes installed storage capacity were usable as of May 2026.
He also demanded accountability for the reported financial allocations to support strategic food reserves and the operations of 45 registered licensed buying companies.
“These allocations and arrangements must be assessed against actual purchases, timely payments to farmers and usable storage capacity. Announcements must produce measurable relief.”
The Minority Chief Whip further proposed that schools, universities, hospitals, prisons and the Ghana Armed Forces prioritise locally produced food to create predictable demand for farmers.
He also called for urgent investment in storage facilities, food processing, transportation and loan restructuring for affected farmers.
Mr Annoh-Dompreh urged the relevant parliamentary committees to investigate the crisis and visit affected farming communities and markets.
He demanded that the Minister for Food and Agriculture provide Parliament with data on unsold produce, actual purchases by NAFCO, outstanding payments to farmers and available storage capacity.
He also called for a time-bound national intervention plan backed by transparent procurement, independent audits and regular reports to Parliament.
“Our farmers do not need sympathy alone; they need buyers. Our market women need functioning markets and consumers with purchasing power.”
The Minority Chief Whip urged Parliament to rise above partisan considerations and act urgently to safeguard agricultural livelihoods and national food security.
